newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The cabinet is to decide soon on proposals to limit international access to SA through 25 airports and a host of border posts amid national intelligence fears of a flood of illegal weapons from Angola.

- National Party (NP) negotiating supremo Roelf Meyer was stripped of his powers as secretary-general in a major shake-up of the party leadership announced by national leader FW de Klerk on Wednesday. De Klerk said Meyer would be freed to pursue the creation of a new political movement and the post of secretary-general would be scrapped.

- Cooperation talks between the European Union (EU) and SA suffered a setback on Wednesday when negotiators failed to reach agreement on the terms under which SA firms would be allowed to tender for projects funded by the European development fund.
- Gencor has increased its stake in Colombian nickel producer Cerro Matoso SA (CMSA) in a 730 million rand deal that will add about $90 million a year to revenues at current nickel prices.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Boland Bank BOLJ.J, soon to merge with NBS, clinched the lucrative contract on Wednesday to support Pick 'n Pay's muchvaunted foray into the financial services sector.
- Ketan Somaia, chief executive of the Dolphin Group, claimed on Wednesday there was a dirty-tricks campaign against him to sabotage the group's rights to develop Mpumalanga's nature parks.

- Eskom, the electricity utility, faced another bitter confrontation with labour on Wednesday in reaction to its decision to sell two decommissioned power stations without consulting the affected unions.

- Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau has delayed the announcement of a new chairman for Eskom because the government and unions are torn between two contenders, businessman Reuel Khoza and executive deputy chairman of New Africa Investments (Nail), Cyril Ramaphosa, government sources said on Wednesday.
SAKE BEELD
- The South African institutions such as Southern Life, Sanlam, Standard Bank and Fedsure have pledged more than two billion rand to a black empowerment project.

- The trade and industry parliament portfolio committee on Wednesday sharply criticised the Small Business Development Corporation (SBDC) for still lending money mainly to white small business developments, to the disadvantage of black businesses.
- Pick 'n Pay announced on Wednesday that it had chosen Boland Bank as its partner to expand into the financial services sector.
THE STAR
- Representatives of the warring parties in Zaire plan to meet for the first time in Cape Town on Thursday, President Nelson Mandela said.
- From railway clerk to self-made millionaire, Louis Luyt is one of South Africa's most controversial sports administrators.

- Former Springbok rugby coach Andre Markgraaff, admitting that he was always public enemy number one after he axed former Springbok captain Francois Pienaar, has appealed to the public to forgive him and unite in support of the new rugby management team.
- Once again, when the National Party is faced with one of the most serious threats to its survival, it has turned to Roelf Meyer to guide it out of its darkness.
